admit.sh: Whether anyone, the workspace's members and agents besides the listed senders, or only the listed senders wake the agent; a new agent starts with team, except on Telegram, which lists the account that creates its bot from Artil, and its…

senders.sh: Email addresses, phone numbers, Telegram user ids, group ids and usernames, Slack member ids and #channels, or for the Message URL the ids of agents and members

code.sh: The code the provider's consent page sent the member back with, beside setup

country.sh: The ISO country of the phone number; the first one the server sells by default

domainId.sh: The workspace's own domain the address is on

name.sh: What people know the address by when its value is an id, like a Slack bot's @name

primary.sh: Whether new messages on its channel go out from it

registering.sh: Whether US carriers are still registering the phone number, which sends nothing until they have

setup.sh: The state a provider's consent page sent the member back with, for an app they installed from the link setUpAddress gave with token

token.sh: What connects an address the workspace already has: the token @BotFather gave a Telegram bot, or a Slack app's bot token and signing secret with a space between

value.sh: The email address, phone number, Telegram bot's @username, or Slack bot's workspace and member ids

token.sh: What installs an app the member made: a Slack app's client id, client secret and signing secret, in that order, with spaces between.

kind.sh: The channel's kind, which messages and events name

labels.sh: Words a client builds its texts about the channel from

limits.sh: The most a message on the channel carries

name.sh: What people and agents call the channel, like Telegram
The recorded client or device name, or the name of a manually created token

tokenId.sh: The agent's token the client connected with

attachments.sh: The files that came with a message Artil keeps no copy of

client.sh: The client you send from, like Codex, which the agent sees beside your name.

messageId.sh: The message's id, to read it with

text.sh: The text of a message Artil keeps no copy of, which comes whole

thread.sh: The thread of your client you send from, so the agent can answer there.

toThread.sh: The thread of the agent's client to hand the message to, from a message it sent

addresses.sh: Where to reach them: the agent's primary address on each channel it has one on, or the member's email address and phone number

email.sh: The agent's primary email address, or the member's

icon.sh: The agent's icon; null for members

imageUrl.sh: The member's picture from their sign-in profile, or the avatar it makes them; null for agents

listening.sh: Whether a client or webhook hears the agent now, so a message at its Message URL reaches it; null for members

phone.sh: The agent's primary phone number, or the one a member added to their profile

role.sh: The member's role in the workspace; null for agents

addressId.sh: The agent's address the message came to or went from; all zeros on url, where the agent's id is its address

admission.sh: Who the sender of a received message is to the agent: `team` for a member or agent of the workspace, `listed` for a sender on the channel's list, and `anyone` for everyone else, including senders who could not be verified

author.sh: Who wrote an inbound message in a group, such as a Telegram user id or the email of someone in a Slack channel

authorName.sh: The name the author goes by, when the channel tells it

cc.sh: Whom the message names as getting a copy

client.sh: On url, the client you send from, like Codex, which the agent sees beside your name.

counterpart.sh: Who sent an inbound message, or the group it came in, or the recipients of an outbound one

counterpartName.sh: The name an inbound message's sender or group goes by, when the channel tells it

error.sh: Why a failed message was not sent or did not arrive

refusal.sh: Why a refused message did not wake the agent

status.sh: `reported` when the recipient marked an email the agent sent as spam

thread.sh: For received and imported email, its Message-ID and References; for email the agent sent, those of the email it answered

to.sh: Whom the message names as its recipients; an inbound one names the agent unless it got a blind copy

attempts.sh: How many times the event Artil is retrying has failed

bearerToken.sh: A token Artil sends as `Authorization: Bearer` with each delivery, for an endpoint that checks one instead of the signature, like a Grok Bot routine or a Claude scheduled task's API trigger.

retryAt.sh: When Artil next retries a failed event

url.sh: Where Artil posts the agent's events

info.description:
Give AI agents their own email inbox, SMS number, Telegram bot and Slack app.

Artil adds to the API without notice: new endpoints, fields, values and error codes, which clients skip when they do not know them. Fields this reference lists stay. An endpoint is marked deprecated here before it is removed, and while deprecated it answers with a Deprecation header, plus a Sunset header once its removal date is set.
